response.sql: WITH per AS (SELECT transref, AVG(anlycount) AS avg_cnt FROM sentimentandfundamentals GROUP BY transref), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_cnt) AS overall_avg FROM per WHERE avg_cnt IS NOT NULL), kept AS (SELECT p.transref, p.avg_cnt, o.overall_avg FROM per p CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE p.avg_cnt > o.overall_avg), kept_avg AS (SELECT AVG(avg_cnt) AS kept_avg FROM kept), ranked AS (SELECT k.transref, k.avg_cnt AS avg_anlycount, k.avg_cnt - k.overall_avg AS diff_from_overall_avg, k.avg_cnt - ka.kept_avg AS diff_from_kept_avg FROM kept k CROSS JOIN kept_avg ka), r2 AS (SELECT *, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY diff_from_kept_avg DESC NULLS LAST) AS rnk FROM ranked) SELECT transref, avg_anlycount, diff_from_overall_avg, diff_from_kept_avg FROM r2 WHERE rnk <= 10 ORDER BY diff_from_kept_avg DESC NULLS LAST

assumptions.assumption: The overall average is the mean of per-transaction averages, excluding transactions whose average is NULL (all anlycount values missing); each transaction counts equally regardless of how many rows it has.

'How far above' is a signed difference (per-transaction average minus the reference average), without rounding. Because the kept set is above the overall average, the difference from the kept average can be negative.
Ties with the 10th row are included using RANK() on the difference from the kept average.
